speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic. I understand you are experiencing chronic bladder discomfort and frequent urination; to help me identify the cause, can you tell me how long these symptoms have been occurring and if you experience pain or blood in your urine?

speaker: Patient
text: 40-year-old female. The patient reports a 5-month history of worsening bladder discomfort, which is relieved by voiding. She mentions an increased frequency of urination, voiding 10–15 times during the day and waking up 2–3 times at night to void. She denies any involuntary loss of urine. Attempts to manage the discomfort with reduced fluid intake and NSAIDs have provided minimal relief. She also reports recent painful intercourse.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Interstitial Cystitis/Bladder Pain Syndrome.

The clinical picture of chronic bladder pain relieved by voiding, significant urinary frequency (including nocturia), and dyspareunia in a 40-year-old female is classic for Interstitial Cystitis. While a Urinalysis is often the first step to rule out infection, your symptoms and the lack of relief with NSAIDs strongly point towards this diagnosis. Please confirm if you have tried any pelvic floor physical therapy, as that is often part of the management plan.
